transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump says artificial intelligence companies can self-regulate their developments.
He held a meeting with dozens of AI industry leaders at the White House yesterday.
NPR's Emily Fang reports Trump says some of the leaders reached a voluntary agreement.
Trump posted a one-page document that CEOs from six of the big AI companies that were
present signed, and in that document it said companies would broadly monitor their models
and make sure they don't hack other systems, for example, but the document didn't offer
details on how this would work.
And asked if this document was enforceable, Trump said it was "morally binding," so
the question remains whether powerful private companies can be trusted to follow through
in perpetuity.
NPR's Emily Fang reporting.
Former Justice Department Special Counsel Jack Smith testified on Capitol Hill yesterday.
He defended his investigations of President Trump and said he would not be intimidated
by threats of prosecution, and bears Ryan Lucas reports.
In his appearance before the Senate Judiciary Committee, Jack Smith said he stands by his
decision to bring charges against President Trump, and that politics played no role in
the investigation.
The charges against President Trump were the result of the evidence.
Evidence of election interference, obstruction, and the mishandling of classified documents.
Republicans repeatedly went after Smith, accusing him of conducting a partisan investigation
to get Trump and Republicans more broadly.
Some echoed Trump's calls for Smith himself to be prosecuted, to which Smith replied,
"I will not be silenced by continued threats of prosecution from the president or others."
The more than four-hour hearing ended where it began with a bitter partisan divide.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
It is illegal in the U.S. to make a baby using gene-edited human embryos.
But NPR's Rob Stein reports at least two start-ups are hoping to change that.
Origin genomics in New York City and preventive bio in San Francisco are trying to produce
enough evidence to convince regulators that it would be safe to use modified embryos for
reproduction.
The companies say gene-editing embryos could help millions of babies from being born with
rare but devastating genetic disorders.
Critics, however, warn it may never be safe and worry that allowing gene-editing of human
embryos for any reason could open the door to someone trying to go further and create
designer babies.
Rob Stein, NPR News.
An airport in Saudi Arabia and the airline fly Dubai report there was a disturbance on
a flight that landed today at Tabuk Airport.
Upon landing, the captain and co-pilot both sustained injuries and were hospitalized.
Details are not clear.
NPR's learned the Israeli prime minister is holding a security consultation now.
This is NPR.
The U.S. Supreme Court will allow the Trump administration to continue sending migrants
to countries where they have no ties.
The unsigned order comes as the high court prepares to hear full arguments on the case
in December.
The Trump administration says this policy helps the U.S. remove dangerous migrants from the
country.
Opponents say migrants deported like this suffer and face detention, rape, and disappearances.
Forecasters say the remnants of a hurricane that hit Mexico are contributing to heavy
rain in the U.S.
Flood watches and warnings are up from Arizona to Illinois.
The Texas Panhandle has some flash flood warnings.
Alaska's Fat Bear Week has a new winner.
His name is Backpack.
He's estimated to weigh more than 1,000 pounds.
Alaska Public Media's Ava White has more.
Backpack, also known as number 89, got his nickname because he'd hold onto his mama's
back as they crossed the Brooks River in Katmai National Park and Preserve.
He's now 20 years old.
Backpack has gained so much weight over the summer that his before and after photos look
like totally different brown bears.
Katmai Park Ranger Sarah Bruce says Backpack isn't an aggressive bear.
He's more of like a stoic presence on the river.
He doesn't really get into drama or cause any upset in the hierarchy.
He holds his own very quietly.
His victory was declared Tuesday evening after he triumphed in the competition that drew a
record number of voters from around the world.
For NPR News, I'm Ava White in Anchorage.
I'm Corova Coleman, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: President Trump meets with AI industry leaders; companies sign voluntary agreement to self-regulate
Former Justice Department Special Counsel Jack Smith testifies before Senate Judiciary Committee about Trump investigations
Two biotech startups seek to legalize gene-edited human embryos for reproduction in the United States
Disturbance on flight at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia injures captain and co-pilot
U.S. Supreme Court allows Trump administration to continue deporting migrants to countries with no ties
Remnants of hurricane hitting Mexico cause heavy rain and flood warnings across southwestern United States
Backpack, a 20-year-old brown bear, wins Alaska's Fat Bear Week competition with record voter turnout
